name: Sensory Overload
summary: A state of being flooded by more sensory input (sound, light, touch, smell, crowding) than the brain can process at once, which can produce distress, shutdown, or meltdown.
triggers: Loud, layered, or sudden noises (alarms, crowds, machinery)
Uncomfortable textures, clothing tags, or unexpected touch

remedies.text: Reduce sensory input immediately — dim lights, lower noise, move to a quieter space — rather than pushing through the environment
Noise-canceling headphones or earplugs in known loud environments
Occupational therapy sensory integration approaches to build tolerance and coping strategies over time
Give advance notice about sensory-heavy events (fireworks, assemblies, crowded stores) so the person can prepare or opt out
